title: Lenny White - Wikipedia
notes: Born Leonard White III, 19 December 1949, Queens; self-taught; first gig with Jackie McLean, who recommended him for Bitches Brew; Freddie Hubbard's Red Clay; Return to Forever 1972-76; Venusian Summer, Big City; Twennynine; Azteca; produced Echoes of an Era; 'one of the founding fathers of jazz fusion'; Magnificent Seven dedicated to Tony Williams and others.

title: Romantic Warrior - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded February 1976 at Caribou Ranch; White on drums and percussion; his Sorceress 'starts with a funky riff'; the band's best seller, gold.

title: Return to Forever - Wikipedia
notes: Drummers: Airto Moreira (1972-73), Steve Gadd (1973), Lenny White (1973-76 and reunions), Gerry Brown (1977). 'Gadd was unwilling to tour with the band ... Lenny White ... replaced Gadd and Lewis.'

title: Land of the Midnight Sun (album) - Wikipedia
notes: White drums on track 2, the title track; Steve Gadd on 1, Alphonse Mouzon on 5. July and August 1975.

title: Todd Bishop, Notes on a Lenny White performance (cruiseshipdrummer.com, 2019)
notes: Cymbals reversed on a right-handed kit (ride on the left); singles and doubles; 'tune oriented'; 'big accompanying statements that were not always on the same grid as the primary groove'; Tony Williams in the 1960s a formative influence.

title: Todd Bishop, Groove o' the day: Lenny White - Red Clay
notes: Measured 64-70 bpm, the second bar of the vamp a little faster; 'really on the front of the beat'; a double-time feel in the sax solo at the same tempo. No notation of the groove.

title: Modern Drummer, 'The Magician' transcription by Marc Atkinson (preview)
notes: Preview only: 'he plays openhanded, utilizing his left hand on the hi-hat and right hand on the snare, and even riding with his left hand.'
